assumptions: Customer wants login required, not a specific auth table; the policy does not name one.
Endpoints reaching invoices are judged through their table reads, as the check documents.
Severity critical is appropriate for an invoices data leak; customer did not state one.
confusions: The skill says to scope by tables for named tables, but the check catalogue example for object.auth_required shows tables only as a scope; it was clear enough but the 'judges endpoints reaching the tables' wording could mean direct reads only. Unclear whether a function-mediated read counts.
xano policy parse echoed the whole file on success and gave no explicit OK line; I took exit 0 as success.
The skill's Honesty section forbids predicting outcomes as results, but the brief asks for a plan that states what will be reported; I labelled the export finding as a prediction.
wished_for: A way to run xano policy evaluate in this step so the export finding could be quoted rather than predicted (the brief forbids it here).
A template or recipe for 'data of table X never returned in full' (row cap plus auth) so the paging gap has a documented pairing.
why_confidence: The auth rule correctly scopes to invoices and will catch an unauthenticated endpoint that reads the table. It does not stop authenticated full-table reads or cross-org reads, and it is advisory, so it blocks nothing until the owner changes it. The existing export endpoint already violates it and I left it unchanged.
